<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

```python
place_ids(input_ids: object, device: _core.Device) -> 'evoxc.Tensor'
```

Part of [`evoxc_hf.pipeline`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/)

Also available as `evoxc_hf.place_ids`.

Copy token ids onto `device` — explicit, one-step placement.

The ids half of the device-resident recipe (its counterpart is
`place_params`): a non-cpu executable rejects *every* host input at the
run boundary by design, ids included, so both sides must be placed
explicitly — `evoxc_hf.run(exe, evoxc_hf.place_params(params, device),
evoxc_hf.place_ids(ids, device))`.

Host ids are cast to `int32` — the same single documented id coercion
`run` performs on a host array, so the placed tensor matches the
graph's `evoxc.int32` ids input instead of failing dtype-strictly at the run
boundary. An `evoxc.Tensor` is **not** re-typed (a tensor's data is
never silently rewritten): it is validated and moved with the explicit
`Tensor.to(device)`, which is a no-op when it already lives there.

## Parameters

- `input_ids` · `object` — `(batch_size, seq_len)` integer token ids — a host array
  (any integral dtype) or an `evoxc.Tensor`.

- `device` · `_core.Device` — the target `evoxc.core.Device` (e.g. `Device("cuda", 0)`).

## Returns

- `'evoxc.Tensor'` — evoxc.Tensor: an `int32` ids tensor on `device`.

## Raises

- `TypeError` — `device` is not an `evoxc.core.Device`.

- `evoxc.ShapeError` — `input_ids` is not 2-D.

- `evoxc.DTypeError` — `input_ids` (array or Tensor) is not integral.
